sentences.text: It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 15.2.2016, one Prakash, a 42 year old died.

3. It is not in dispute that the Insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.
4.

The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident which has resulted in the death of Prakash.
The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award a total compensation of Rs.10,86,000/-.

5. In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.
6. Since the deceased was aged 42 and was self- employed, 25% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.11,875/-.
Claimants are wife, two children and mother of the deceased and therefore, 1/4th of the income has to deducted towards personal expenses.
7. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.8907/-.
8. As the deceased was aged 42 years, a multiplier of '14' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.14,96,376/- (8,907 x 12 x 14) towards "loss of dependency".

9. The claimants being the wife, children and mother of the deceased, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,76,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

10. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 14,96,376  2. Loss of Consortium 1,76,000
3 . Conventional Heads 33,000

Total 17,05,376 Smt Jyothi vs K R Venkatesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192703606/
3 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.17,05,376/- as against Rs.10,86,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

However, it is made clear that the enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
12.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
13. The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 513 days in filing the appeal.
14. The deposit and release of the compensation amount awarded shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
15. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
16. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
